correctness.rationale: From the initiating paper’s r=1/2 utility, the unilateral action payoff difference is delta_i times the sum of opposing-community spins divided by two. Every pure equilibrium belongs to exactly one of four classes: both opposing-community sums nonzero; only A nonzero; only B nonzero; both zero. The first class exists iff the two role imbalances share a strict sign and contributes exactly two globally flipped profiles. Each one-sided tie contributes the complete nonbalanced action set of the free part when the strict side’s induced magnetization is zero. The last contributes the two balanced-binomial factors. This yields the exact formula for all a,b>=1. Nonnegative terms prove universal role existence iff both sizes even, with attainable exact extrema; independent symmetric role signs give the role-random probability. Direct unilateral-payoff exhaustive tests from the supplied Python path passed 400 role composition comparisons over 102400 profiles, plus 25 extrema/existence and 25 rational probability checks; finite checks corroborate, not prove all-size theorem. No unproved limiting extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: Full-text primary model, earlier complete-graph paper, the previously cited 80-page thesis, and the later signed-network generalization were assessed by their hypotheses and implications, not matching titles. They define the problem, prove conditional existence or full-network homogeneous results, but do not imply the role-parameterized exhaustive equilibrium formula on K_(a,b). The central-binomial double-tie factor is a known simple balance count and not claimed separately as new. A nearby published majority-coloring summary was compared and found unrelated to the full strategic constraints. Semantic-index queries disclosed no stronger coverage. Specialist-priority uncertainty remains and is explicitly recorded; a missing source is not equated with proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Undiscovered specialist research may have independently derived the complete bipartite four-stratum equilibrium count.

value.rationale: Mixed strategic complements and substitutes can destroy pure equilibrium, so exact role-robust existence is a motivated structural problem. The infinite complete-bipartite family models two fully cross-interacting communities, and parity of both sizes is proved to be the sharp condition for every arbitrary heterogeneous assignment of conformist or anti-conformist roles to support equilibrium. The exact count also distinguishes exponentially numerous tie strata from two strict-majority equilibria and yields quantitative extremal and randomized robustness laws. This is a meaningful complete classification, not an arbitrary sample size, parameter tweak, or mere recovery of known balance identities.
